title: Bezalel's hands (Exodus 35:30–35)
hook: the first person filled with the Spirit in the Bible is a craftsman

segments.voice: Yesterday: hesed, loyal love, and God's name proclaimed right after the calf: merciful and gracious. Your line: slow to anger.

Quick question. In the Bible, who is the first person God is said to fill with his spirit? A prophet, you'd guess. A priest. Moses, maybe. Pharaoh once said the spirit of God was in Joseph, but the first time the text says God filled someone, it's none of those. It's a man named Bezalel. And the spirit fills him not to preach or work miracles, but to work gold and silver and bronze, cut stones, carve wood, and make beautiful things. The tabernacle, the tent where God would dwell among the people, needs building. And God picks the person who's good with his hands.
screen: `WHO WAS FILLED FIRST?` → `NOT A PROPHET. NOT A PRIEST.` → `A CRAFTSMAN.`

segments.voice: Moses tells the people, in the King James Bible, that God has called Bezalel by name, "And he hath filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship." Wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and then, without a pause, workmanship. Skill with your hands sits in the same breath as wisdom. In this book, making something well is a spiritual gift. Bezalel isn't alone. He's given a partner, Oholiab, from another tribe, and God put it in their hearts to teach. So the gift isn't hoarded. It's passed on, workshop style, to everyone the text calls wise-hearted: women spinning blue and purple yarn, men carving acacia wood, jewelers setting stones. Whole sections of Exodus go to curtains and clasps, lampstands and loops, measured down to the cubit. People skip those chapters. The Bible takes its time there, as if to say: this matters too. His name is lovely as well: Bezalel means in the shadow of God. And notice the timing. This comes right after the golden calf. The people's gold went into an idol; now gold, given freely, goes into a place for God to dwell. Same material, same hands, two directions. Christians have taken this passage as a blessing on every kind of craft: the stonemasons of the great cathedrals, quilters and carpenters, the person who fixes your car well. In this story, the spirit of God fills a workshop before it fills a pulpit.
screen: `WISDOM, AND WORKMANSHIP.` · `PUT IN HIS HEART TO TEACH.` · `IN THE SHADOW OF GOD.` · `GOLD FOR A CALF, GOLD FOR A TENT.` · then, large: `FILLED WITH THE SPIRIT OF GOD.`

segments.voice: Make something small with care: fold a cloth perfectly, wash one cup slowly all the way around, or set three things on a table so they look right together. Pay attention to the material in your hands, its weight and its texture, as if the work itself were an offering. If you pray, you can offer it.
Bezalel's hands. The craftsman of the tabernacle, the first person the Bible says was filled with the spirit of God, for wisdom and for workmanship.
Your line: craft is spiritual. Even curtains and clasps can be holy work. Four hundred days, and counting.

howItsDone: Many Christians see craft and good work as a way of honoring God, and churches have long blessed builders, artists and artisans; some congregations hold services blessing tools or the work of people's hands.

notes: 'First person said to be filled with the spirit of God': Exodus 31:3 is the first use of the phrase 'filled with the spirit of God'. Pharaoh earlier says the Spirit of God is in Joseph (Genesis 41:38). The script says 'said to be filled', per the index; confirm the claim is fair.
Bezalel 'in the shadow (protection) of God': standard lexicon reading; confirm.
Oholiab is spelled 'Aholiab' in the KJV; the script uses the more common modern spelling.
'Women spinning blue and purple yarn' from Exodus 35:25–26; confirm.
Services blessing tools or work: e.g., Plough Monday, Labor Day blessings; confirm the general wording in howItsDone.

Audit (10% sample): the hook's 'first person filled with the spirit... none of them' clashed with day 370, which quotes Pharaoh calling Joseph 'a man in whom the Spirit of God is' (Genesis 41:38); hook now names that and makes the claim about God filling someone (Exodus 31:3). Myth item said the tabernacle chapters come after the calf, but the plans (25–31) come before; reworded to the building. Closing line 'You don't have to be in a pulpit to be filled with the spirit' read as a belief claim to the listener; now describes the story.
